hero.eyebrow: Open source · End-to-end encrypted · Native on three platforms
hero.title: Copy on your Mac.
hero.description: Free, open source, and end-to-end encrypted — text, images, and files flow seamlessly between your Mac, Windows, and Linux machines. Direct on the same Wi-Fi, NAT hole-punching across networks. No account ever.

features.title: Feels like the OS clipboard — but cross-platform, searchable, auditable.

h1.title: The relay only sees ciphertext.
h1.lede: Content is encrypted at the source and decrypted only on your devices. Keys live in the system keyring and never leave your machine. Open source, auditable.
h1.b1Desc: XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD — encrypted in transit and at rest.
h1.b2Desc: No email, no phone number — just two devices exchanging a public key.
h1.b3Desc: AGPL-3.0 open source. Read and verify the crypto yourself.

h2.title: Not just LAN. Not bound to one network.
h2.lede: First-class on Windows, macOS, and Linux — built on Rust + Tauri, not an Electron wrapper. Direct on the same Wi-Fi; NAT hole-punching across networks; encrypted relay as a fallback.
h2.b1Desc: Rust + Tauri — fast launch, low footprint, integrates with the OS.
h2.b2Desc: Devices on the same network connect peer-to-peer with millisecond latency.
h2.b3Desc: Across home/office/internet — automatic hole-punching, encrypted relay if it fails.

h3.title: Quick Panel, full-text search, CLI — all included.
h3.lede: A keyboard-shortcut overlay to preview history; millisecond search across tens of thousands of items; a headless CLI for terminals, SSH, and tmux. Deeper than its surface lets on.
h3.b1Desc: Shortcut overlay with inline previews for text, links, images, code, and files.
h3.b2Desc: Search the full history in milliseconds — even with tens of thousands of entries. The index stays encrypted on disk.
h3.b3Desc: GUI features, one command — runs headlessly for terminals, SSH, scripts, and tmux workflows.

more.f1Desc: ⌘C / Ctrl-C to copy, ⌘V / Ctrl-V to paste — no muscle-memory taxes. An extension of the system clipboard, not another app.
more.f4Desc: Reconnects automatically after Wi-Fi switches, sleep/wake, and brief disconnects. No re-pairing.
more.f6Desc: Copy on one device, paste on another. Large files use streaming transfer so they never have to fit in memory.
more.f5Desc: Manage paired devices, presence and per-device sync preferences. Lost a device? Revoke it from any paired one.
more.f7Desc: Skips clipboard items flagged by password managers and the system keychain — your tokens won't sync to other devices.
more.f9Desc: Default 30 days; switch to 7 / forever; clear by device or type; wipe history at any time.

comparison.title: Why not iCloud? Why not self-hosted?
comparison.subtitle: If any of these matters to you — iCloud Universal Clipboard and "run-your-own-server" tools won't cut it.

transport.label: Direct on Wi-Fi, relay across networks

comparison.footnote: Comparison based on public information as of 2026-05. Spotted something off? Open an issue on GitHub.

howItWorks.title: Pair once. After that, just copy and paste.
howItWorks.step1Desc: Devices exchange a public key once, locally — no cloud account, no email. Generate a short-lived invitation code on one device; the new device joins with the code and the space passphrase.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Content is encrypted at the source. Ciphertext flows over a direct P2P link (same Wi-Fi or NAT hole-punching). When direct fails, it falls back to an encrypted relay. Even a malicious relay only sees ciphertext.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Decryption happens only on your devices. Local history and the search index are encrypted at rest. Connections recover automatically after Wi-Fi switches, sleep/wake, or brief disconnects.

item1.q: Why not just iCloud Universal Clipboard?
item1.a: If you only use Apple devices, don't need history, and fully trust Apple's closed-source E2E encryption — iCloud is fine. The moment you add a Windows or Linux machine, want a searchable history, or want to verify the encryption yourself, you need something else.

item2.q: Why not a self-hosted clipboard sync (e.g. ClipCascade)?
item2.a: Self-hosted means you operate a server. UniClipboard works out of the box — direct P2P first, encrypted relay only as a fallback. You never have to run any infrastructure.

item3.q: Does it work fully offline / LAN-only?
item3.a: Yes. Devices on the same Wi-Fi connect directly without going through the relay. Even if the relay is unreachable, devices on the same network keep syncing.

item4.q: Where does my clipboard history actually live?
item4.a: Only on your devices. Local storage is encrypted at rest with a key that never leaves the system keyring. No UniClipboard server ever receives or stores your clipboard content.

item5.a: Not yet. The current release focuses on getting Windows, macOS and Linux right. Mobile is on the roadmap, but OS-level clipboard permissions and background-execution limits need to be solved first — we'll ship it when it's ready, not before.

item6.q: Will AGPL-3.0 affect me using it inside a company?
item6.a: No. AGPL only kicks in if you modify the source and then redistribute it as a network service. Installing it for personal or team use is no different from any other free app — you don't have to open-source any of your company's code.

footer.thanksDesc: Cross-device clipboard sync — end-to-end encrypted, open source, auditable. Flows seamlessly between your own machines, without any cloud account in between.
